reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general oxide integrity and stress effects in FeNiCuAlX HEAs without Mg, but provides no specific support for MgO formation, Mg-rich intermetallic precipitation, or their role in oxide disruption in Mg-containing alloys. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: MgO forms a continuous protective oxide film early in oxidation
Thermally activated diffusion causes Mg segregation and Mg-rich intermetallic nucleation beneath the oxide
Intermetallic growth induces stress and structural discontinuities in the oxide layer
Oxide disruption by intermetallics reduces corrosion and oxidation resistance
Cyclic vs. continuous oxidation can delineate time/temperature service boundaries for this mechanism
